A is the better fit because `settings/resolver.ts:12` already owns the defaults, and the path I traced shows `ui/report-view.ts:30` reading values that have already been resolved there. If the new setting lives in the resolver, the report view gets it the same way it gets every other setting, and each setting has one read path and one place that owns its default. A view-local settings object would add a second source for defaults next to the resolver. The view would then have to merge two settings shapes, and the two defaults could drift apart. I've recorded resolver ownership as decided.

Next is what the setting controls. Report filters currently stay active when you switch workspaces and can hide rows in the new workspace. What should happen to active filters on a workspace switch?
A) Always reset them to the resolved defaults. No user choice, so this is a fixed behavior change.
B) A resolver-backed setting chooses between "reset on switch" and "keep across workspaces", with "reset" as the default.
C) Remember filters per workspace, so each workspace restores its own last filters.
D) Other - name it.

Recommendation: B. It is the setting you asked for, and it uses the resolver we just chose. Defaulting to "reset" fixes the hidden-rows problem out of the box. Users who rely on carrying filters across workspaces can still choose "keep". C solves a different problem, per-workspace memory, and needs new storage that nothing in the traced path provides.

Reusing the resolver keeps a single source of truth: `settings/resolver.ts:12` already owns defaults, and `ui/report-view.ts:30` already consumes its resolved settings. The new setting can follow that same path without introducing a view-local object whose defaults or values could drift.

What should the new setting’s **default behavior** be when switching workspaces?

A) Clear report filters so they cannot hide rows in the new workspace.
B) Preserve report filters, matching today’s behavior; users can opt into clearing them.
C) Other — name it.

Recommendation: A - it directly addresses the hidden-row problem, while the setting still lets users choose preservation.
